localBiteReport: The week of September 4–10, 2026 is bringing the first clear signs of the fall transition to Choctawhatchee Bay, with water temperatures at 87°F and enormous bait concentrations moving through the system. Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters reports that schools of greenies (scaled sardines) are pushing from deeper open water into bayous, flats, bridge areas, and roll-downs, which is starting to concentrate predators and improve overall activity on the bay's flats. The redfish flat-sight-fishing bite is described as improving and expected to build further over the coming weeks as the fall mullet run gets underway — Capt. Nelson anticipates the first meaningful slot redfish opportunity arriving in the second or third week of September. This is a transitional window: the deep-summer doldrums are easing, but the full fall inshore push for reds, trout, and flounder hasn't fired yet — the next week or two should accelerate things considerably.
